profiles.notes: Joint specialist medical training offered with the University of Zimbabwe, which awards each of these six qualifications.

requirements.label: Prior medical degree
requirements.details: The joint IUM and University of Zimbabwe specialist route requires an MBChB or equivalent medical qualification from a recognised higher education institution.

source.title: IUM · 2027 General Information for Prospective Students · pp. 63–64, School of Medicine

requirements.label: Completed internship
requirements.details: Provide evidence that you completed a medical internship.

source.title: IUM · 2027 General Information for Prospective Students · pp. 63–64, School of Medicine

requirements.label: Registered practice experience
requirements.details: Applicants must have practised as registered medical practitioners for at least two years.

source.title: IUM · 2027 General Information for Prospective Students · pp. 63–64, School of Medicine

requirements.label: Registration eligibility in both countries
requirements.details: Meet the registration criteria of both the Health Professions Council of Namibia and the Medical and Dental Practitioners Council of Zimbabwe.

source.title: IUM · 2027 General Information for Prospective Students · pp. 63–64, School of Medicine

requirements.label: Evidence of funding for the full training period
requirements.details: Demonstrate sufficient funds for university fees, the research project and personal living costs throughout training.

source.title: IUM · 2027 General Information for Prospective Students · pp. 63–64, School of Medicine

requirements.label: Additional specialist qualification
requirements.details: A postgraduate diploma in the chosen specialty strengthens the application. It is optional.

source.title: IUM · 2027 General Information for Prospective Students · pp. 63–64, School of Medicine

requirements.label: Merit selection and possible assessment
requirements.details: The selection committee assesses merit under the university and programme rules. It may use an interview and a knowledge test.

source.title: IUM · 2027 General Information for Prospective Students · pp. 63–64, School of Medicine

requirements.label: Degree completion and joint training locations
requirements.details: The University of Zimbabwe awards the NQF Level 9 qualification jointly taught with IUM. Full-time studies normally last four years: Part I lasts 12 months (maximum 24), and Part II lasts 36 months (maximum 48). Candidates must complete and defend a dissertation. Both descriptions put Part I in Zimbabwe. Pages 63 and 64 name different countries for Part II; confirm that placement with the faculty.
